title: Heads up: UK retail sales to test the case for further BOE rate hikes
summary: The UK retail sales release will be one of the main items to watch out for in the economic calendar today, especially after the latest inflation and labour market figures have given the BOE plenty to think about ahead of its November meeting. For the September report, retail sales are expected to fall by 0.1% on the month, following a 0.5% increase in August. Meanwhile, retail sales are expected to rise by 1.0% annually - a slowdown from 2.4% previously. The numbers might not be all too interesting on the surface, but they will matter to the broader context in shaping the BOE outlook. UK headline annual inflation climbed to 3.5% in September, with core annual inflation also picking up to 2.8%. That is hardly reassuring for the BOE, especially with policymakers already having to contend with elevated energy prices and the risk of more persistent price pressures. Meanwhile, the labour market gave us a bit of a surprise earlier this week. The unemployment rate surprisingly fell to 4.7%, while real wage growth nudged slightly higher to 3.7%. The numbers might be affected by data quality issues with the ONS but they reflect a modest bounce in labour market conditions regardless. Having said that, the details are less rosy with job vacancies continuing to decline, suggesting that hiring demand is losing momentum. And in any case, one report doesn't make a trend. The UK labour market has been showing signs of softness this year and I would be remiss if I didn't point out that fact.
